briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the Daily Climate Briefing for November 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 COP31 Talks Collapse Amid Unprecedented Temperature Spikes
sections.content: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) has ended in failure without reaching a final agreement following intense friction over phasing out fossil fuels [20, 99]. Negotiations came to a dramatic close after a coalition of nations rejected the proposed 'Antalya Agreement,' leaving critical marine conservation measures also in limbo [124, 130]. In response, Pope Leo XIV expressed deep regret and concern over the summit's conclusion without strong commitments, urging world leaders to take immediate action [99, 113, 125]. Meanwhile, global daily surface temperatures surged to 2.24°C above pre-industrial levels, marking an unprecedented six consecutive days exceeding the 2°C threshold and escalating a sense of crisis worldwide [127].

sections.title: ⚠️ Extreme Weather Backlash Hits Daily Life and Ecosystems
sections.content: Driven by climate change, increased atmospheric moisture and prolonged atmospheric stagnation are reshaping traditional heavy rainfall patterns, triggering a series of destructive extreme downpours [6]. In San Francisco, a leading high-tech city, record-breaking torrential rain led to sewage backups and severe downtown flooding [17]. In South Korea, shifting ocean temperatures have disrupted the winter supply of yellowtail, while globally, the intersection of climate change and trade practices is threatening banana supplies, dealing a direct blow to grocery prices and food security [7, 110].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Local Governments' Carbon Neutrality Efforts Confront Policy Disconnects
sections.content: The Incheon Institute proposed that expanding civic reward systems and localized community engagement—placing citizens at the core of policy implementation—are vital to achieving carbon neutrality by 2045 [23, 50, 58]. However, policy contradictions have surfaced on the ground: in Jeju, the provincial government's carbon neutrality budget surged by 84%, while administrative city budgets declined by 27%, all while coal briquette subsidy programs persist [38, 46, 48]. Furthermore, carbon-intensive sectors such as steel are struggling to maintain industry viability amid transition burdens and trade pressures, underscoring the urgent need for structured institutional support [53].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Expansion and Innovative Agricultural Adaptation
sections.content: Community-driven renewable energy deployment led by local governments is gaining momentum, with Pyeongchang County signing an agreement for a 150 MW solar power project and Daegu's Seo-gu securing national and municipal funding to expand support coverage [76, 88, 90]. In agriculture, local breakthrough strategies are emerging: Gunwi County received the Grand Prize for Agricultural Technology Dissemination Innovation by introducing the new 'Golden Ball' apple variety, while Gyeonggi Province is advancing farmer-led 'Climate-Smart Agricultural Administration' [9, 13]. Additionally, leveraging the COP summit, the Korea Forest Service established cross-border forestry cooperation achievements, including an agreement to launch the 'Korea-Honduras REDD+ Cooperation Center' [1, 19].

briefing.closing: Amid ongoing gridlock in international negotiations, community- and ground-level actions for climate adaptation and energy transition have become all the more crucial. That concludes today's climate briefing.
